# Custom resources

Generated from `config/crd/bases/*.yaml` -- the same schema `kubectl explain` and `kubectl apply --validate` read. Five namespaced kinds in `spawnery.cloud/v1alpha1`.

A few fields are Kubernetes' own types, embedded by reference rather than declared in this repository: they appear as a single row naming the type and linking to [the Go package reference for `k8s.io/api/core/v1`](https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/api/core/v1) instead of being expanded here.

- [Network](#network)
- [ServerGroup](#servergroup)
- [ProxyGroup](#proxygroup)
- [Server](#server)
- [ScaleBoost](#scaleboost)

## Network

**Scope:** Namespaced &nbsp;&nbsp; **Plural:** `networks` &nbsp;&nbsp; **Short names:** `mcnet`

Network is the root resource of a Minecraft network.

### What `kubectl get` shows

<div style="overflow-x: auto;"><table>
<thead><tr><th>Column</th><th>Type</th><th>JSONPath</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>Server Groups</td><td>integer</td><td><code>.status.serverGroups</code></td></tr>
<tr><td>Players</td><td>integer</td><td><code>.status.onlinePlayers</code></td></tr>
<tr><td>Age</td><td>date</td><td><code>.metadata.creationTimestamp</code></td></tr>
</tbody></table></div>

### spec

NetworkSpec describes one Minecraft network. Exactly one Network may exist per namespace; further ones are rejected with an Accepted=False condition.

<div style="overflow-x: auto;"><table>
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Required</th><th>Default</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>commands</code></td><td>object</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Commands opens in-game commands that reach past the operator&#x27;s own objects. Absent, all of them are off.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>commands.execute</code></td><td>boolean</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Execute lets an administrator on a proxy run a console command on one server or on every server of a group with /cloud execute. Off, the operator refuses every such request.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>defaults</code></td><td>object</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Defaults are inherited by all groups of this network.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>defaults.feedFormat</code></td><td>string</td><td align="center"></td><td><code>&lt;gray&gt;»&lt;/gray&gt; &lt;gradient:aqua:green&gt;Spawnery&lt;/gradient&gt; &lt;dark_gray&gt;|&lt;/dark_gray&gt; &lt;gray&gt;$EVENT_MESSAGE</code></td><td>FeedFormat is the line the agent&#x27;s chat output wears: announcements about the cloud and replies to a <code>/cloud</code> command alike.<details><summary>more</summary>MiniMessage. <code>$EVENT_MESSAGE</code> is replaced by what the line has to say; everything around it is yours.<br><br>Changing it rolls no pod and takes effect within a resync interval. A value that MiniMessage cannot parse makes the agent send the message alone.</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>defaults.imagePullSecrets</code></td><td>array</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>ImagePullSecrets are attached to every managed pod.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>defaults.imagePullSecrets[].name</code></td><td>string</td><td align="center"></td><td><code></code></td><td>Name of the referent. This field is effectively required, but due to backwards compatibility is allowed to be empty. Instances of this type with an empty value here are almost certainly wrong. More info: <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/names/#names">https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/names/#names</a></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>defaults.minecraftVersion</code></td><td>string</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>MinecraftVersion documents the version the images of this network carry.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>defaults.resources</code></td><td><a href="https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/api/core/v1#ResourceRequirements">ResourceRequirements</a> (Kubernetes, not expanded here)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Resources are the default container resources.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>defaults.scheduling</code></td><td>object</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Scheduling is the default pod placement.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>defaults.scheduling.affinity</code></td><td><a href="https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/api/core/v1#Affinity">Affinity</a> (Kubernetes, not expanded here)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Affinity expresses scheduling preferences and constraints.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>defaults.scheduling.nodeSelector</code></td><td>map[string]string</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>NodeSelector restricts pods to nodes carrying all these labels.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>defaults.scheduling.tolerations</code></td><td><a href="https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/api/core/v1#Toleration">[]Toleration</a> (Kubernetes, not expanded here)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Tolerations allow pods onto tainted nodes.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>forwardingSecretRef</code></td><td>object</td><td align="center">&#10003;</td><td></td><td>ForwardingSecretRef names the Secret holding the Velocity modern forwarding secret under the key &quot;secret&quot;.<details><summary>more</summary>Generate the value at random. Every pod carries a salted eight-byte digest of it in the spawnery.cloud/forwarding-hash label, readable by anyone who can read pods, so a memorable secret can be guessed offline. <tr><td><code>forwardingSecretRef.name</code></td><td>string (length &gt;= 1)</td><td align="center">&#10003;</td><td></td><td>Name of the referenced object.</td></tr>

<tr><td><code>scheduling.hostPortRange.max</code></td><td>integer (int32) (1-65535)</td><td align="center">&#10003;</td><td></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>scheduling.hostPortRange.min</code></td><td>integer (int32) (1-65535)</td><td align="center">&#10003;</td><td></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>update</code></td><td>object</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Update is how the network&#x27;s groups change over to a new spec.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>update.maxConcurrentChangeovers</code></td><td>integer (int32) (&gt;= 1)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>MaxConcurrentChangeovers is how many server and proxy groups may change over at the same time. A group changing over runs one server more than its size until its last stale server is gone; a change that reaches every group at once needs that room for every group at once. Unset means no cap.</td></tr>

Read by observers; the operator writes it and reads nothing back from it.

<tr><td><code>conditions[].message</code></td><td>string (length 0-32768)</td><td align="center">&#10003;</td><td></td><td>message is a human readable message indicating details about the transition. This may be an empty string.</td></tr>

<tr><td><code>conditions[].type</code></td><td>string (length 0-316; pattern <code>^([a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?(\.[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?)*/)?(([A-Za-z0-9][-A-Za-z0-9_.]*)?[A-Za-z0-9])$</code>)</td><td align="center">&#10003;</td><td></td><td>type of condition in CamelCase or in foo.example.com/CamelCase.</td></tr>

**Scope:** Namespaced &nbsp;&nbsp; **Plural:** `servergroups` &nbsp;&nbsp; **Short names:** `mcgroup`

### spec

ServerGroupSpec describes a group of Minecraft servers.

<div style="overflow-x: auto;"><table>

<tr><td><code>scaling</code></td><td>object</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Scaling configures slot-based scaling. Ephemeral only. Editing it replaces no server.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>scaling.maxReplicas</code></td><td>integer (int32) (&gt;= 1)</td><td align="center">&#10003;</td><td></td><td>MaxReplicas caps the number of servers.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>scaling.minReplicas</code></td><td>integer (int32) (&gt;= 0)</td><td align="center">&#10003;</td><td></td><td>MinReplicas is the number of servers kept running at all times.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>scaling.scaleDownStabilizationSeconds</code></td><td>integer (int32) (&gt;= 0)</td><td align="center"></td><td><code>300</code></td><td>ScaleDownStabilizationSeconds is how long a server must be empty before it is eligible for scale-down.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>scaling.spareSlots</code></td><td>integer (int32) (&gt;= 0)</td><td align="center">&#10003;</td><td></td><td>SpareSlots is the number of free player slots kept available, counted in playable seats when the group sets playableSlots.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>scheduling</code></td><td>object</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Scheduling overrides Network.spec.defaults.scheduling.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>scheduling.affinity</code></td><td><a href="https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/api/core/v1#Affinity">Affinity</a> (Kubernetes, not expanded here)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Affinity expresses scheduling preferences and constraints.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>scheduling.nodeSelector</code></td><td>map[string]string</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>NodeSelector restricts pods to nodes carrying all these labels.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>scheduling.tolerations</code></td><td><a href="https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/api/core/v1#Toleration">[]Toleration</a> (Kubernetes, not expanded here)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Tolerations allow pods onto tainted nodes.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>storage</code></td><td>object</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Storage configures the PVC. Persistent and OnDemand only.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>storage.accessModes</code></td><td>array of string</td><td align="center"></td><td><code>[ReadWriteOnce]</code></td><td>AccessModes are immutable once set.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>storage.annotations</code></td><td>map[string]string</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Annotations are copied onto each data claim when it is created, e.g. for a volume autoresizer&#x27;s per-claim ceiling. Existing claims are not changed.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>storage.backend</code></td><td>string (one of: Claim, ObjectStore)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Backend is where a member&#x27;s world lives between runs. Claim, the default, keeps it on a PersistentVolumeClaim per member. ObjectStore keeps it in the object store configured for the operator (chart value worldSync) and gives /data from a directory on the node that runs the member; it needs type OnDemand and keep, and synchronises exactly what keep matches. It also needs game images with spawnery&#x27;s agent 0.24.0 or later, whose bootstrapper holds the server until the world is on disk: an older or a custom image without it starts on a half-downloaded world and can corrupt it. Size, storageClassName, accessModes and annotations are ignored under ObjectStore and stay valid for switching back. The backend may change either way; nothing is moved across.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>storage.keep</code></td><td>array of string (at least 1 item(s))</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Keep lists the paths on the data claim, relative to /data, that survive a start. When set, each start first deletes everything on the claim that no entry matches, then renders and copies as before. Unset, everything is kept.<details><summary>more</summary>An entry is a path whose segments may use * and ? (path.Match per segment). A matched directory is kept whole. Mount points, their parent directories and the root lost+found are never deleted. The start is refused when a path no entry keeps is, or holds, a level.dat* file, a region directory or an .mca file, unless extraFiles and extraPlugins ship every file and directory at and below it at the same path, which the copy then writes back, or a replace entry matches it.</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>storage.replace</code></td><td>array of string (at least 1 item(s))</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Replace lists paths on the data claim, relative to /data, that the sources own. A start deletes them like any other path keep does not match, without the check for worlds, and the copy after it writes back what extraFiles and extraPlugins ship now. Meant for world templates the server copies from and never loads, whose shipped form changes between releases. Same syntax as keep; where both match, keep wins. Needs keep.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>storage.size</code></td><td>object (pattern <code>^(\+|-)?(([0-9]+(\.[0-9]*)?)|(\.[0-9]+))(([KMGTPE]i)|[numkMGTPE]|([eE](\+|-)?(([0-9]+(\.[0-9]*)?)|(\.[0-9]+))))?$</code>)</td><td align="center">&#10003;</td><td></td><td>Size of each new claim. Raising it grows existing claims up to the new size (needs allowVolumeExpansion on the StorageClass); lowering it changes only claims created afterwards and never shrinks one. A claim larger than this, grown by hand or by an autoresizer, is left alone.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>storage.storageClassName</code></td><td>string</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>StorageClassName is immutable once set.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>substitution</code></td><td>object</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Substitution fills placeholders in the files the entrypoint copies from extraPlugins and extraFiles. See Substitution.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>substitution.prefix</code></td><td>string (pattern <code>^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$</code>)</td><td align="center">&#10003;</td><td></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>terminationGracePeriodSeconds</code></td><td>integer (int64) (&gt;= 1)</td><td align="center"></td><td><code>60</code></td><td>TerminationGracePeriodSeconds is the time the pod gets to save its world.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>type</code></td><td>string (one of: Ephemeral, Persistent, OnDemand)</td><td align="center">&#10003;</td><td></td><td>Type selects ephemeral, persistent or on-demand operation. Immutable.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>update</code></td><td>object</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Update configures the rolling update. Ephemeral only.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>update.maxStaleSeconds</code></td><td>integer (int32) (&gt;= 0)</td><td align="center"></td><td><code>0</code></td><td>MaxStaleSeconds forces an active drain of stale servers after this many seconds. 0 means stale servers are never actively emptied.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>update.maxUnavailable</code></td><td>integer (int32) (&gt;= 1)</td><td align="center"></td><td><code>1</code></td><td>MaxUnavailable is how many servers may be draining or terminating at the same time because of a generation change.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>update.minAvailable</code></td><td>integer (int32) (&gt;= 1)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>MinAvailable is how many servers must stay joinable while the group changes over: Ready, registered, door open, and not on their way out, of either generation. The group builds one extra server at a time to keep it. Unset keeps no floor beyond one Ready server of the current generation.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>update.strategy</code></td><td>string (one of: RollingUpdate, WhenEmpty)</td><td align="center"></td><td><code>RollingUpdate</code></td><td>Strategy is how stale servers are replaced.</td></tr>
</tbody></table></div>

### status

Read by observers; the operator writes it and reads nothing back from it.

<div style="overflow-x: auto;"><table>
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Required</th><th>Default</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>boostedReplicas</code></td><td>integer (int32)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>BoostedReplicas is how much of this group&#x27;s current floor comes from ScaleBoost objects rather than from spec.scaling.minReplicas.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>changeover</code></td><td>string (one of: , Waiting, Begun, Deferred)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Changeover is this group&#x27;s changeover as the network&#x27;s budget sees it; written by its own reconcile and read by its siblings&#x27;.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>conditions</code></td><td>array</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Conditions follow the standard Kubernetes condition contract.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>conditions[].lastTransitionTime</code></td><td>string (date-time)</td><td align="center">&#10003;</td><td></td><td>lastTransitionTime is the last time the condition transitioned from one status to another. This should be when the underlying condition changed.  If that is not known, then using the time when the API field changed is acceptable.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>conditions[].message</code></td><td>string (length 0-32768)</td><td align="center">&#10003;</td><td></td><td>message is a human readable message indicating details about the transition. This may be an empty string.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>conditions[].observedGeneration</code></td><td>integer (int64) (&gt;= 0)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>observedGeneration represents the .metadata.generation that the condition was set based upon. For instance, if .metadata.generation is currently 12, but the .status.conditions[x].observedGeneration is 9, the condition is out of date with respect to the current state of the instance.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>conditions[].reason</code></td><td>string (length 1-1024; pattern <code>^[A-Za-z]([A-Za-z0-9_,:]*[A-Za-z0-9_])?$</code>)</td><td align="center">&#10003;</td><td></td><td>reason contains a programmatic identifier indicating the reason for the condition&#x27;s last transition. Producers of specific condition types may define expected values and meanings for this field, and whether the values are considered a guaranteed API. The value should be a CamelCase string. This field may not be empty.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>conditions[].status</code></td><td>string (one of: True, False, Unknown)</td><td align="center">&#10003;</td><td></td><td>status of the condition, one of True, False, Unknown.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>conditions[].type</code></td><td>string (length 0-316; pattern <code>^([a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?(\.[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?)*/)?(([A-Za-z0-9][-A-Za-z0-9_.]*)?[A-Za-z0-9])$</code>)</td><td align="center">&#10003;</td><td></td><td>type of condition in CamelCase or in foo.example.com/CamelCase.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>consecutiveFailures</code></td><td>integer (int32)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>ConsecutiveFailures counts *rounds* in which at least one server failed to start, with no success since. One pass adds one however many servers it saw fail.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>failureStreakKey</code></td><td>string</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>FailureStreakKey identifies what the servers counted in consecutiveFailures started with: the desired pod hash, the configOverlay ConfigMap&#x27;s resourceVersion and the spawnery.cloud/retry annotation. The streak is reset when any of them moves, and by nothing else. Opaque; compare it, never parse it.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>freeSlots</code></td><td>integer (int32)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>FreeSlots is the number of seats a proxy can send a player to right now: the free playable seats of servers that are Ready, in the proxies&#x27; routing tables, accepting joins, and rendered under the group&#x27;s current spec. It is the scaler&#x27;s input.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>lastFailureAt</code></td><td>string (date-time)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>LastFailureAt is the newest status.failedAt this group has counted. It is what makes the count idempotent across resyncs, and the instant the backoff window runs from.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>observedGeneration</code></td><td>integer (int64)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>ObservedGeneration is the spec generation this status was computed from.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>onlinePlayers</code></td><td>integer (int32)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>OnlinePlayers is the sum of players across all ready servers.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>phase</code></td><td>string</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Phase says whether players can join: Ready means the group&#x27;s *floor* is met -- spec.replicas for a persistent group, spec.scaling.minReplicas for an ephemeral one -- not that every server the scaler decided to run is up. Compare readyReplicas against replicas for that, or see the Progressing condition.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>pinnedReplicas</code></td><td>integer (int32)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>PinnedReplicas is the size an Exact ScaleBoost holds this group at, which can be 0. Absent while no pin holds.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>pinnedUntil</code></td><td>string (date-time)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>PinnedUntil is when that pin ends. Absent without a pin, and for a pin without an end.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>readyReplicas</code></td><td>integer (int32)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>ReadyReplicas is the number of servers in phase Ready.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>replicas</code></td><td>integer (int32)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Replicas is the number of Server objects owned by this group.</td></tr>
</tbody></table></div>


## ProxyGroup

**Scope:** Namespaced &nbsp;&nbsp; **Plural:** `proxygroups` &nbsp;&nbsp; **Short names:** `mcproxy`

ProxyGroup is the Velocity layer of a network.

### What `kubectl get` shows

<div style="overflow-x: auto;"><table>
<thead><tr><th>Column</th><th>Type</th><th>JSONPath</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>Phase</td><td>string</td><td><code>.status.phase</code></td></tr>
<tr><td>Ready</td><td>integer</td><td><code>.status.readyReplicas</code></td></tr>
<tr><td>Address</td><td>string</td><td><code>.status.address</code></td></tr>
<tr><td>Players</td><td>integer</td><td><code>.status.connectedPlayers</code></td></tr>
<tr><td>Age</td><td>date</td><td><code>.metadata.creationTimestamp</code></td></tr>
</tbody></table></div>

### spec

ProxyGroupSpec describes the Velocity layer of a network.

<div style="overflow-x: auto;"><table>
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Required</th><th>Default</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>attributes</code></td><td>map[string]string</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Attributes is what plugins are told about this group. See GroupAttributes. Editing it replaces and restarts nothing.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>changeoverStage</code></td><td>integer (int32)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>ChangeoverStage orders this group&#x27;s changeover against the network&#x27;s other groups: a group waits while any group of a lower stage is still changing over. Groups of one stage change over together, within Network.spec.update.maxConcurrentChangeovers.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>config</code></td><td>object</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Config are the rendered Velocity settings.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>config.motd</code></td><td>string</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Motd is shown in the server list. Editing it rolls the group&#x27;s proxies.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>config.onlineMode</code></td><td>boolean</td><td align="center"></td><td><code>true</code></td><td>OnlineMode is whether the proxy authenticates players with Mojang.<details><summary>more</summary>Turning it off lets any client connect under any name; the backends run online-mode=false and do not catch it. It is not the backends&#x27; proxies.velocity.online-mode, which stays true either way.<br><br>Editing it rolls the group&#x27;s proxies.</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>config.playerLimit</code></td><td>integer (int32) (&gt;= 1)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>PlayerLimit is the network-wide player limit of one proxy.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>configOverlay</code></td><td>object</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>ConfigOverlay names a ConfigMap whose keys are configuration files to merge over the rendered defaults — &quot;server.properties&quot;, &quot;paper-global.yml&quot;, &quot;paper-world-defaults.yml&quot; or &quot;velocity.toml&quot;, in the target&#x27;s own dialect.<details><summary>more</summary>It outranks the rendered defaults and is outranked by the operationally critical fields.<br><br>A key the receiving program does not declare is refused, since Paper and Velocity silently ignore it. The declared keys come from each program&#x27;s captured default configuration, so a Paper or Velocity bump can refuse a new key until that capture is updated. server.properties keys are not checked.</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>configOverlay.name</code></td><td>string (length &gt;= 1)</td><td align="center">&#10003;</td><td></td><td>Name of the referenced object.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>displayName</code></td><td>string (length 0-64)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>DisplayName is what this group is called where a person reads it: a scoreboard, a chat message, a playtime key.<details><summary>more</summary>The operator carries it and reads none of it. Empty, a plugin shows the group&#x27;s own name.</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>drain</code></td><td>object</td><td align="center"></td><td><code>{timeoutSeconds: 300}</code></td><td>Drain bounds how long existing sessions may run out on proxy replacement.<details><summary>more</summary>It reaches the pod as terminationGracePeriodSeconds, so editing it replaces every proxy of the group. A drain already in flight picks up the new deadline.</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>drain.timeoutSeconds</code></td><td>integer (int32) (&gt;= 1)</td><td align="center">&#10003;</td><td></td><td>TimeoutSeconds is the upper bound for the drain.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>env</code></td><td>array</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Env are extra environment variables for the proxy container, appended to the ones the operator sets. A name may not begin with SPAWNERY_. JVM options go in JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS.<details><summary>more</summary>Editing it replaces every proxy of the group. A valueFrom reference is digested, not its value: rotating the Secret or ConfigMap reaches only new pods.</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>env[].name</code></td><td>string</td><td align="center">&#10003;</td><td></td><td>Name of the environment variable. May consist of any printable ASCII characters except &#x27;=&#x27;.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>env[].value</code></td><td>string</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Variable references $(VAR_NAME) are expanded using the previously defined environment variables in the container and any service environment variables. Double $$ are reduced to a single $, which allows for escaping the $(VAR_NAME) syntax: i.e. &quot;$$(VAR_NAME)&quot; will produce the string literal &quot;$(VAR_NAME)&quot;. <tr><td><code>expose</code></td><td>object</td><td align="center">&#10003;</td><td></td><td>Expose makes the proxies reachable from outside the cluster.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>expose.clusterIP</code></td><td>object</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>ClusterIP configures type ClusterIP.</td></tr>

<tr><td><code>extraPlugins</code></td><td>object</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>ExtraPlugins names a volume whose plugins and their configuration are copied into this group&#x27;s servers on every start. See ExtraPlugins.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>extraPlugins.claimName</code></td><td>string (length &gt;= 1)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>ClaimName is a PersistentVolumeClaim in this object&#x27;s own namespace.<details><summary>more</summary>It must be ReadWriteMany, even for a single-replica group: a ReadWriteOnce claim would leave the second server Pending on a volume affinity error.</details></td></tr>

<tr><td><code>mounts</code></td><td>array</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Mounts are extra ConfigMap, Secret and PersistentVolumeClaim mounts.</td></tr>

<tr><td><code>mounts[].name</code></td><td>string (length &gt;= 1)</td><td align="center">&#10003;</td><td></td><td>Name of the volume inside the pod.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>mounts[].persistentVolumeClaim</code></td><td>object</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>PersistentVolumeClaim source. See MountClaim.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>mounts[].persistentVolumeClaim.claimName</code></td><td>string (length &gt;= 1)</td><td align="center">&#10003;</td><td></td><td>ClaimName is a PersistentVolumeClaim in this object&#x27;s own namespace.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>mounts[].persistentVolumeClaim.writable</code></td><td>boolean</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Writable mounts the claim read-write. It defaults to false.<details><summary>more</summary>Nothing coordinates writers: two groups that both write the same claim get what two processes writing one filesystem get.<br><br>Flipping it replaces the group&#x27;s servers.</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>mounts[].secret</code></td><td><a href="https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/api/core/v1#SecretVolumeSource">SecretVolumeSource</a> (Kubernetes, not expanded here)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Secret source.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>mounts[].subPath</code></td><td>string</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>SubPath mounts one file or one subdirectory of the source instead of the whole of it, so that MountPath can be a file.<details><summary>more</summary>Without it, a mount whose path names a file gets a *directory* there holding the source&#x27;s keys as separate files.<br><br>**A ConfigMap or Secret mounted through subPath does not update** in a running pod; without subPath it does, eventually. No edit to a ConfigMap&#x27;s contents rolls anything.</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>networkRef</code></td><td>object</td><td align="center">&#10003;</td><td></td><td>NetworkRef names the Network this group belongs to. Immutable.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>networkRef.name</code></td><td>string (length &gt;= 1)</td><td align="center">&#10003;</td><td></td><td>Name of the referenced object.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>replicas</code></td><td>integer (int32) (&gt;= 1)</td><td align="center">&#10003;</td><td></td><td>Replicas is the number of proxy pods.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>resources</code></td><td><a href="https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/api/core/v1#ResourceRequirements">ResourceRequirements</a> (Kubernetes, not expanded here)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Resources overrides Network.spec.defaults.resources.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>routing</code></td><td>object</td><td align="center">&#10003;</td><td></td><td>Routing configures the fallback groups.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>routing.fallbackGroups</code></td><td>array of string (at least 1 item(s))</td><td align="center">&#10003;</td><td></td><td>FallbackGroups is the ordered try-list on join and on drain.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>scheduling</code></td><td>object</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Scheduling overrides Network.spec.defaults.scheduling.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>scheduling.affinity</code></td><td><a href="https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/api/core/v1#Affinity">Affinity</a> (Kubernetes, not expanded here)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Affinity expresses scheduling preferences and constraints.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>scheduling.nodeSelector</code></td><td>map[string]string</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>NodeSelector restricts pods to nodes carrying all these labels.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>scheduling.tolerations</code></td><td><a href="https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/api/core/v1#Toleration">[]Toleration</a> (Kubernetes, not expanded here)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Tolerations allow pods onto tainted nodes.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>substitution</code></td><td>object</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Substitution fills placeholders in the files the entrypoint copies from extraPlugins and extraFiles. See Substitution.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>substitution.prefix</code></td><td>string (pattern <code>^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$</code>)</td><td align="center">&#10003;</td><td></td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>update</code></td><td>object</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Update bounds how long a draining proxy may wait for its players.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>update.maxStaleSeconds</code></td><td>integer (int32) (&gt;= 0)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>MaxStaleSeconds disconnects the players left on a draining proxy after this many seconds. 0, the default, means a drain waits for its players: the proxy takes no new connections and stops once empty.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>update.transfer</code></td><td>object</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Transfer moves players to another proxy instead of waiting for them.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>update.transfer.forceAfterSeconds</code></td><td>integer (int32) (&gt;= 0)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>ForceAfterSeconds is how long a leaving proxy waits before it transfers players who have not changed server, counted from when its agent first sees it leaving. Default 120; keep it below drain.timeoutSeconds and any maxStaleSeconds.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>update.transfer.forceGroups</code></td><td>array of string</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>ForceGroups limits the forced transfer to players on servers of these server groups; everyone else moves only when they change server. Empty forces in every group.</td></tr>
</tbody></table></div>

### status

Read by observers; the operator writes it and reads nothing back from it.

<div style="overflow-x: auto;"><table>
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Required</th><th>Default</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>address</code></td><td>string</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Address is where players connect.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>changeover</code></td><td>string (one of: , Waiting, Begun, Deferred)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Changeover is this group&#x27;s changeover as the network&#x27;s budget sees it; written by its own reconcile and read by its siblings&#x27;.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>conditions</code></td><td>array</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Conditions follow the standard Kubernetes condition contract.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>conditions[].lastTransitionTime</code></td><td>string (date-time)</td><td align="center">&#10003;</td><td></td><td>lastTransitionTime is the last time the condition transitioned from one status to another. This should be when the underlying condition changed.  If that is not known, then using the time when the API field changed is acceptable.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>conditions[].message</code></td><td>string (length 0-32768)</td><td align="center">&#10003;</td><td></td><td>message is a human readable message indicating details about the transition. This may be an empty string.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>conditions[].observedGeneration</code></td><td>integer (int64) (&gt;= 0)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>observedGeneration represents the .metadata.generation that the condition was set based upon. For instance, if .metadata.generation is currently 12, but the .status.conditions[x].observedGeneration is 9, the condition is out of date with respect to the current state of the instance.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>conditions[].reason</code></td><td>string (length 1-1024; pattern <code>^[A-Za-z]([A-Za-z0-9_,:]*[A-Za-z0-9_])?$</code>)</td><td align="center">&#10003;</td><td></td><td>reason contains a programmatic identifier indicating the reason for the condition&#x27;s last transition. Producers of specific condition types may define expected values and meanings for this field, and whether the values are considered a guaranteed API. The value should be a CamelCase string. This field may not be empty.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>conditions[].status</code></td><td>string (one of: True, False, Unknown)</td><td align="center">&#10003;</td><td></td><td>status of the condition, one of True, False, Unknown.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>conditions[].type</code></td><td>string (length 0-316; pattern <code>^([a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?(\.[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?)*/)?(([A-Za-z0-9][-A-Za-z0-9_.]*)?[A-Za-z0-9])$</code>)</td><td align="center">&#10003;</td><td></td><td>type of condition in CamelCase or in foo.example.com/CamelCase.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>connectedPlayers</code></td><td>integer (int32)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>ConnectedPlayers is the sum of players across all proxies.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>observedGeneration</code></td><td>integer (int64)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>ObservedGeneration is the spec generation this status was computed from. It advances on a refused pass too; check Degraded beside it.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>phase</code></td><td>string</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Phase is derived from the proxy pods and conditions.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>readyReplicas</code></td><td>integer (int32)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>ReadyReplicas is the number of proxies that passed the ready gate.</td></tr>

## Server

**Scope:** Namespaced &nbsp;&nbsp; **Plural:** `servers` &nbsp;&nbsp; **Short names:** `mcsrv`

Server is a single running Minecraft server instance.

### What `kubectl get` shows

<div style="overflow-x: auto;"><table>
<thead><tr><th>Column</th><th>Type</th><th>JSONPath</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>Group</td><td>string</td><td><code>.spec.groupRef.name</code></td></tr>
<tr><td>Phase</td><td>string</td><td><code>.status.phase</code></td></tr>
<tr><td>Players</td><td>integer</td><td><code>.status.players</code></td></tr>
<tr><td>Slots</td><td>integer</td><td><code>.status.slots</code></td></tr>
<tr><td>Registered</td><td>boolean</td><td><code>.status.registered</code></td></tr>
<tr><td>Age</td><td>date</td><td><code>.metadata.creationTimestamp</code></td></tr>
</tbody></table></div>

### spec

ServerSpec describes one running Minecraft server instance. It is created and owned by a ServerGroup and is not meant to be edited by hand.

<div style="overflow-x: auto;"><table>
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Required</th><th>Default</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>forceStop</code></td><td>boolean</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>ForceStop kills this server&#x27;s pod at once, with no drain and a grace period of one second: its players lose their connection and the world loses whatever it had not saved. Set by the agent endpoint&#x27;s force-stop request, which only a proxy may send.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>groupGeneration</code></td><td>integer (int64)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>GroupGeneration is the metadata.generation of the group at creation time. A server whose value is behind the group&#x27;s is stale.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>groupRef</code></td><td>object</td><td align="center">&#10003;</td><td></td><td>GroupRef names the owning ServerGroup.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>groupRef.name</code></td><td>string (length &gt;= 1)</td><td align="center">&#10003;</td><td></td><td>Name of the referenced object.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>hold</code></td><td>boolean</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Hold keeps this server against every automatic removal: a rolling update does not retire it, and neither the demand rule nor a lowered maxReplicas deletes it. It stays until it ends by itself. Set by the agent endpoint&#x27;s unretire request; a node drain still moves it, and a retire request still retires it.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>key</code></td><td>string</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Key is the caller&#x27;s name for the world this member carries, and it is set for a member of an OnDemand group and for no other server. Like Ordinal, it lets a Server say what kind of member it is once its group is gone.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>number</code></td><td>integer (int32) (&gt;= 0)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Number is which of its group&#x27;s servers this is, counted the way a person counts: the second hub is 2. The group assigns it once, at creation, and it is given out again only after this server is gone.<details><summary>more</summary>A persistent server&#x27;s Number equals its Ordinal. Zero means unnumbered: a server older than this field, or ordinal zero of a persistent group. A reader then falls back to the server&#x27;s name.</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ordinal</code></td><td>integer (int32) (&gt;= 0)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Ordinal is the stable index of a persistent server. Unset for ephemeral servers, whose names carry a random suffix instead.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>podHash</code></td><td>string</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>PodHash is podspec.DesiredServerHash at the moment this server was created: a digest of everything the operator would render for it. The group compares it against a freshly computed one to decide whether this ordinal is running the current spec.<details><summary>more</summary>Empty means adopt, never stale: the group stamps the current hash onto such a server and orders no takedown.</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>retire</code></td><td>boolean</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Retire asks this server to stop taking joins and empty out, without its players being moved. The ServerGroup controller sets it during a rolling update, and an administrator through the agent endpoint&#x27;s retire request. A server counts against spec.update.maxUnavailable while this is true.</td></tr>
</tbody></table></div>

Producers of specific condition types may define expected values and meanings for this field, and whether the values are considered a guaranteed API. The value should be a CamelCase string. This field may not be empty.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>conditions[].status</code></td><td>string (one of: True, False, Unknown)</td><td align="center">&#10003;</td><td></td><td>status of the condition, one of True, False, Unknown.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>conditions[].type</code></td><td>string (length 0-316; pattern <code>^([a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?(\.[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?)*/)?(([A-Za-z0-9][-A-Za-z0-9_.]*)?[A-Za-z0-9])$</code>)</td><td align="center">&#10003;</td><td></td><td>type of condition in CamelCase or in foo.example.com/CamelCase.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>drainStartedAt</code></td><td>string (date-time)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>DrainStartedAt is when the server entered phase Draining. Drives the drain deadline.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>failedAt</code></td><td>string (date-time)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>FailedAt is when the server entered phase Failed. Drives the retention.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>phase</code></td><td>string</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Phase is the state machine position: Pending, Starting, Ready, Draining, Terminating or Failed.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>playableSlots</code></td><td>integer (int32)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>PlayableSlots is how many of Slots count as capacity: the plugin&#x27;s figure, else the group&#x27;s spec.playableSlots, else Slots.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>players</code></td><td>integer (int32)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Players is the last reported player count, throttled to protect etcd.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>playersUpdatedAt</code></td><td>string (date-time)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>PlayersUpdatedAt is when Players was last reported by the agent. Counts older than twice the report interval are treated as occupied.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>podName</code></td><td>string</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>PodName is the pod backing this server. Set once the pod was created and never reused for a different pod.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>podUID</code></td><td>string</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>PodUID identifies the pod behind PodName, and so one run of this server apart from the next one under the same name, which a persistent server keeps across restarts. Not cleared when the pod goes.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>readinessLosses</code></td><td>integer (int32)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>ReadinessLosses counts how often this server fell out of Ready. Past the threshold the server is considered broken rather than flapping.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>readySince</code></td><td>string (date-time)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>ReadySince is when the server last entered phase Ready. Drives the reset of the readiness-loss counter.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>registered</code></td><td>boolean</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Registered reports whether the proxies currently know this server.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>retiringSince</code></td><td>string (date-time)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>RetiringSince is when the server entered phase Retiring. It drives spec.update.maxStaleSeconds and nothing else — what marks a server as one this update made unavailable is spec.retire.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>roundEndedAt</code></td><td>string (date-time)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>RoundEndedAt is when the server said its round was over. Nil for one that never did. Stamped while the server still runs, so it survives an operator restart.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>slots</code></td><td>integer (int32)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>Slots is the player capacity reported by the agent.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>startedAt</code></td><td>string (date-time)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>StartedAt is when this server last began trying to become playable: the first pass that accepted it, then the pod creation, and then every entry into phase Starting. It drives the startup deadline, which therefore bounds the current attempt rather than the age of the pod, and also fails a Server whose pod is never created.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>storageResizeError</code></td><td>string</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>StorageResizeError names why the last resize of this server&#x27;s claim failed, or is empty when none did: this operator&#x27;s patch refused by the API server (usually allowVolumeExpansion: false), or a driver failure from the claim&#x27;s ControllerResizeError or NodeResizeError condition.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>storageResizePending</code></td><td>boolean</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>StorageResizePending is true while this server&#x27;s claim carries the FileSystemResizePending condition: the CSI driver has grown the volume and needs the pod restarted before the filesystem follows. Most drivers expand online and never set it.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>wasRegistered</code></td><td>boolean</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>WasRegistered is true once this server has been registered with the proxies during the life of its current pod. A server that fell back to Starting may still have players connected.</td></tr>
</tbody></table></div>


## ScaleBoost

**Scope:** Namespaced &nbsp;&nbsp; **Plural:** `scaleboosts` &nbsp;&nbsp; **Short names:** `boost`

ScaleBoost is extra capacity for a group, for a while.<details><summary>more</summary>It is its own object rather than a field on the group because the operator cannot write a ServerGroup&#x27;s spec, and under GitOps that spec belongs to a file anyway.<br><br>It adds to the group&#x27;s floor and never to its ceiling: spec.scaling. maxReplicas still binds. Its effect shows on the group as status.boostedReplicas.</details>

### What `kubectl get` shows

<div style="overflow-x: auto;"><table>
<thead><tr><th>Column</th><th>Type</th><th>JSONPath</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>Group</td><td>string</td><td><code>.spec.groupRef.name</code></td></tr>
<tr><td>Mode</td><td>string</td><td><code>.spec.mode</code></td></tr>
<tr><td>Replicas</td><td>integer</td><td><code>.spec.replicas</code></td></tr>
<tr><td>Expires</td><td>date</td><td><code>.spec.expiresAt</code></td></tr>
<tr><td>Age</td><td>date</td><td><code>.metadata.creationTimestamp</code></td></tr>
</tbody></table></div>

### spec

ScaleBoostSpec is extra capacity for one group, for a while.

<div style="overflow-x: auto;"><table>
<thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Required</th><th>Default</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>expiresAt</code></td><td>string (date-time)</td><td align="center"></td><td></td><td>ExpiresAt is when this boost stops counting. A boost without one never expires; the tools that create boosts supply a default.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>groupRef</code></td><td>object</td><td align="center">&#10003;</td><td></td><td>GroupRef names the ServerGroup this adds capacity to.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>groupRef.name</code></td><td>string (length &gt;= 1)</td><td align="center">&#10003;</td><td></td><td>Name of the referenced object.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>mode</code></td><td>string (one of: Add, Exact)</td><td align="center"></td><td><code>Add</code></td><td>Mode Add raises the group&#x27;s floor by Replicas; boosts on one group add up. Mode Exact holds the group at exactly Replicas servers, 0 included: the group&#x27;s floor and ceiling both become that number, Add boosts stop counting, and of several Exact boosts the newest wins. Neither lifts spec.scaling.maxReplicas.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>replicas</code></td><td>integer (int32) (&gt;= 0)</td><td align="center">&#10003;</td><td></td><td>Replicas is how many servers to add (Add, at least 1) or to hold the group at (Exact, at least 0).</td></tr>
</tbody></table></div>
